items.title: Mindef sets up integrity system to tackle misconduct and plug leakages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry has launched an integrity complaints system and appointed integrity liaison officers to combat misconduct, financial leakages and abuse of power within the ministry and the armed forces. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiatives were part of broader efforts to strengthen governance, improve accountability and close loopholes that could expose the ministry and the armed forces to integrity breaches. Speaking at the launch of the Ministry of Defence Integrity Day 2026 at Wisma Pertahanan today, Khaled said integrity was particularly important given the ministry's responsibility for managing public funds and strategic defence assets involving billions of ringgit.

items.title: Zahid: Nadma coordinates 159 NGOs for northeast monsoon response
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has coordinated 159 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) at national, state and district levels for the northeast monsoon, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) chairman, said non-uniformed NGOs are coordinated by the Social Welfare Department. 1 on the national disaster management policy and mechanism," he said.

items.title: Father wants transparent probe into son's death at boarding school
items.summary: TAIPING: The father of a Form Three student found dead at a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar yesterday wants a transparent and comprehensive investigation into his son's death. Mohd Idzwan Razali, 48, said the family would leave it to the authorities to determine what had happened. Idzwan said he was informed of his son's death by the police and the school principal about 4pm yesterday.

items.title: Johor extends Visit Johor Year to 2027 with RM24.75mil boost
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor has extended its Visit Johor Year campaign until Dec 31, 2027, with RM24.75 million allocated for 12 tourism initiatives to attract more visitors and boost local businesses. Another RM3 million will fund the third phase of upgrading works at Johor Zoo, while RM2.7 million is allocated for museum and heritage gallery improvements. In addition, RM2.6 million will go towards recreational facilities at forest eco-parks, RM2.5 million in incentives for tourism event organisers and RM1.3 million for Visit Johor 2027 promotions.

items.title: Malaysia looking at RM2 billion defence procurement deal with France
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is looking at defence procurements worth nearly RM2 billion from France, involving four combat search and rescue (CSAR) helicopters and 36 howitzers, following the issuance of letters of intent during French President Emmanuel Macron's recent visit to Malaysia. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the helicopters were estimated to cost RM1.3 billion, while the howitzers were valued at slightly more than RM600 million. One of the key agreements concerns cooperation in developing the local defence industry.

items.title: Tuaran Hospital to add 200 beds, targets specialist status
items.summary: TUARAN: A new clinical block with 200 additional beds will be built at Tuaran Hospital as part of upgrades toward achieving specialist hospital status under the 14th Malaysia Plan (14MP). "The Health Ministry said the plan to upgrade Tuaran Hospital into a specialist hospital to meet the needs of residents in Tuaran and surrounding areas will involve adding beds, specialties, doctors, nurses, ambulance services and parking facilities, alongside project cost and timeline considerations," he said in a statement today. Madius said Tuaran Hospital currently offers permanent specialist services across four fields, involving five medical specialists.

items.title: Singaporean charged with trafficking over 19kg of cannabis
items.summary: IPOH: A Singaporean man was charged at the magistrate's court here with trafficking 19.04kg of cannabis at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport on Nov 8. The charge was read in Mandarin before magistrate Norizan Riduan. According to the charge sheet, Chen is accused of trafficking an estimated 19,040 grammes of cannabis under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.

items.title: Johor doubles subsidised Jualan Kasih locations to 748
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor will more than double the number of subsidised grocery sales locations to 748 next year under a RM30 million allocation in Budget 2027. The expansion, up from 336 locations currently, aims to help households cope with rising living costs. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the Jualan Kasih Johor programme, which began in 2023, will offer a basic necessities package for RM15.

items.title: PAC to begin Sabah Pan Borneo Highway probe next Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) will begin its investigation into Phase 1 of the Pan Borneo Highway Sabah next Wednesday, starting with witnesses from the Works Ministry and the Sabah Public Works Department. PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the committee would call those involved in managing and implementing the project, including officers who had served since it was first planned, to give evidence. Mas Ermieyati said the committee held a 90-minute discussion yesterday with five Sabah member of parliaments.

items.title: Investment surge propels Malaysia's Q3 growth beyond forecasts: analysts
items.summary: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research and CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said growth exceeded the consensus forecast of 5.3 per cent, with services and construction anchoring expansion alongside stronger manufacturing activity. CIMB Research said domestic demand growth eased to 4.8 per cent in the third quarter from 5.1 per cent in the previous quarter, mainly reflecting slower private consumption. "Manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.7 per cent, driven by stronger E&E growth of 16.5 per cent, while non-E&E manufacturing moderated to 3.5 per cent.

items.title: Man shot dead after opening fire at police in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH: A man was shot dead after opening fire at police during an early morning operation on Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan here today. The incident occurred at 2.30am when a team from Bukit Aman and the Perak police headquarters was conducting crime prevention patrols targeting robbery cases in the area. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said police had attempted to stop a car driven by the suspect.

items.title: US company NTEC signs US$100mil coal supply deal with TNB unit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: American energy and mining firm Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) has signed a three-year US$100 million (US$1=RM4.11) agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to Tenaga Nasional Bhd's unit TNB Fuel Services Sdn Bhd, the White House announced on Wednesday. President Donald Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for US companies, Washington said in a statement on its website today. Other regional developments included a proposed US$2 billion project involving US company Latitude Energy and Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara to improve the utilisation of Indonesia's coal resources using US technology, it said.

items.title: MT Global 168 ketamine smuggling case: Tanker owner arrested, Indonesian police confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesian police said Malaysian authorities have arrested the owner of the MT Global 168 tanker, which was intercepted with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine on board. Indonesian National Police (Polri) Narcotics Crime Director Brigadier General Kristian Parluhutan Siagian said Malaysian police had informed them of the arrest. Kristian said Malaysian authorities had found indications that the vessel had repeatedly changed names, allegedly to conceal its identity and involvement in illegal activities.

items.title: Job fulfilment trumps salary in keeping Malaysian workers loyal
items.summary: The proportion of employees planning to remain with their employers rises from 47 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent below their peers to 63 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent above them. The report found that 75 per cent of highly fulfilled employees earning at or below their peers' salaries planned to stay, compared with only 25 per cent of unfulfilled employees earning above their peers. It also highlighted the importance of career progression, with Malaysian employees seeing a median promotion-related salary increase of 14 per cent, 2.8 times the five per cent median increase for routine pay adjustments.

items.title: MMA wants nationwide audit of hospital infrastructure after Sabah power failure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) wants the Health Ministry to conduct an immediate nationwide audit of critical hospital infrastructure following a reported power failure during surgery at a Sabah hospital. Its president, Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan, said the incident, if confirmed, was unacceptable and raised serious concerns over patient safety and the reliability of essential hospital systems. He said reports of recurring air-conditioning breakdowns, electricity and water supply disruptions, and failures of backup power systems were particularly alarming.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 19, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened flat on Thursday, with the benchmark index unchanged from Wednesday's close of 1,566 points, tracking a mixed overnight performance on Wall Street. Meanwhile, Big Caring Group made a weak debut on Bursa Malaysia's Main Market, opening at RM1.05, below its IPO price of RM1.08. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin remained stable at RM258,574, while Ethereum traded at RM7,314.

items.title: Transport costs push Malaysia's inflation higher to 1.9pct in October
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation edged up to 1.9 per cent in October from 1.8 per cent in September, driven mainly by higher transport costs and electricity, gas and fuel prices. The Statistics Department said the transport group recorded the sharpest increase, with inflation rising to 4.2 per cent from 2.5 per cent the previous month. The subgroup recorded inflation of 4.7 per cent in October compared with just 0.1 per cent in September.

items.title: Johor, Singapore fund RM220k study to prepare locals for JS-SEZ jobs
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor and Singapore will jointly fund a RM220,000 study to identify skills demanded by employers in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ). The initiative aims to help local training institutions prepare Johoreans for upcoming job opportunities. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said both sides would contribute RM110,000 each towards the Johor-Singapore Talent and Skill Gap Study.

items.title: Cable theft disrupts services on busy northern rail route
items.summary: Among ETS services, train 9323 recorded the longest delay at 46 minutes, followed by train 9123 (44 minutes), 9343 (37 minutes), 9223 (33 minutes) and 9425 (30 minutes). KTM Komuter Utara services were more severely affected, with train 2809 recording an 80-minute delay, followed by train 2908 (70 minutes) and 2912 (63 minutes). Other affected Komuter services included train 2815 (41 minutes), 2810 (23 minutes) and 2915 (16 minutes).

items.title: Motorcyclist swept away by floodwaters rescued after clinging to tree
items.summary: BENTONG: A motorcyclist was rescued after clinging to an oil palm tree for safety when fast-moving floodwaters swept him off a flooded stretch of Jalan Telemong-Chemomoi near Karak yesterday. Passers-by pulled him to safety using a steel cable at 8pm. Meanwhile, heavy rain yesterday caused flash floods in several low-lying residential areas and business premises in Karak town.

items.title: Johor allocates RM9mil for Islamic programmes
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor will introduce a voluntary weekly fasting programme every Thursday next year to encourage sunnah practices, strengthen mosque activities and foster closer ties between leaders and the public. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said RM6 million had been allocated to strengthen the Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme, which includes communal breaking of fast and Maghrib and Isyak prayers. Another RM3 million will be allocated to continue Semarak Subuh Johor, which encourages congregational dawn prayers.

items.title: WhatsApp group misunderstanding leads to Form Two student beaten, three students detained
items.summary: In the incident at 8am on Nov 13, the victim was allegedly kicked and punched repeatedly in the classroom by the three 15-year-old students. Tangkak police chief Superintendent Mohd Roslan Talib said police received a report on the incident at 12.09am on Nov 14. "Acting on the report, police identified and arrested the three male students suspected of involvement in the incident.

items.title: Two men remanded over RM500,000 goldsmith shop robbery
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Two men suspected of robbing a goldsmith shop in Batu Enam, Gong Badak, of jewellery worth RM500,000 have been remanded for seven days to assist police investigations. Magistrate Nur Akmal Mohd Bakri issued the remand order today, allowing the suspects to be held from Nov 19 to 25. The robbery took place at 10.45am on Nov 12, when the two men, wearing helmets and face coverings, entered the Permata Al-Idrus goldsmith shop.

items.title: Johor Budget 2027 allocates RM3bil for development, people's aid
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johoreans can expect more financial assistance, housing support and cost-of-living relief under the state's RM3.07 billion Budget 2027 tabled today. Themed Johor Maju, Rakyat Sejahtera (Johor advances, people prosper), the budget outlines 284 commitments targeting B40 and M40 households, entrepreneurs, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), farmers and the agriculture sector. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said Johor will channel RM1.53 billion towards development projects next year, accounting for almost half of its total expenditure, to ensure economic growth translates into better living conditions.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines earns World's Best MICE Airline 2026 title
items.summary: Beyond its MICE services, Malaysia Airlines offers extensive destination connectivity, onboard comfort, dining options and flexible booking arrangements to cater to different travel needs. SUPPORTING MICE TRAVEL For organisers managing events involving delegates from different cities and countries, coordinating group travel can be challenging. Through MHcorporate EVENTS, Malaysia Airlines offers a dedicated service to simplify travel arrangements.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower on lack of buying interest
items.summary: The benchmark index opened 6.26 points lower at 1,560.47. CBH Engineering added 2.5 sen to 66 sen, MMAG Holdings went down half a sen to 1.5 sen, while Zetrix AI was flat at 5.5 sen. United Plantations lost 34 sen to RM31.30, Malaysian Pacific Industries shed 24 sen to RM36.16, Kuala Lumpur Kepong shed 14 sen to RM20.66, while Sunway Construction Group fell 11 sen to RM7.43.

items.title: UEM Sunrise earnings beat sparks analyst upgrades
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts have raised their earnings forecasts for UEM Sunrise Bhd after the property developer posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, supported by higher joint venture contributions and improved property development earnings. The group's net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), surged 163.6 per cent to RM48.75 million from RM18.49 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 13.7 per cent to RM474.88 million. CIMB Securities, meanwhile, raised its FY26 core profit forecast by 72 per cent to RM192 million, reflecting higher joint venture earnings and an estimated RM66 million net gain from the disposal of the Jalan Ampang land.

items.title: Malaysia's new vehicle sales climb 3pct to 673,412 units in 10 months
items.summary: Passenger vehicle sales declined seven per cent to 65,362 units, while commercial vehicle sales dropped nine per cent to 5,157 units. For the January-October period, passenger vehicle sales increased four per cent to 630,461 units from 606,443 units previously. In contrast, commercial vehicle sales fell 12 per cent to 42,951 units from 48,884 units.

items.title: Myanmar's army-backed leader says he is reconsidering Asean ties
items.summary: MYANMAR: Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing said on Wednesday his administration was reconsidering the country's relationship with Southeast Asia's regional bloc Asean but would continue discussions with its members. "They are imposing such pressure only on our country," Min Aung Hlaing said. "For Myanmar and Asean to resume normal relations, we will take into consideration Myanmar's stance and the intentions of Asean member countries.

items.title: Train shortage affects Kelana Jaya LRT frequency, says Rapid KL
items.summary: Rapid KL said its engineering team is working to increase the number of operational trains as soon as possible to restore service frequency on the line. Meanwhile, a review of comments on Rapid KL's official Facebook page found that many passengers had expressed dissatisfaction over service disruptions and unusually heavy congestion at several stations, particularly Jelatek LRT station. "Why did the train service stop at Jelatek?

items.title: A six-minute train journey beneath the mountains: The ECRL Genting Tunnel engineering marvel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — For passengers travelling on board the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)، passing beneath the Titiwangsa Range between Gombak in Selangor and Bentong in Pahang may seem like just another part of the journey. Today، the Genting Tunnel holds the distinction of being the longest rail tunnel in both Malaysia and South-east Asia. While passengers traverse the tunnel in just over six minutes، its construction presented a far greater challenge، particularly navigating the varying geological conditions beneath the 300-million-year-old Titiwangsa Range.

items.title: PEOPLElogy’s leaders conference rallies corporate Malaysia to put people first in AI push, as ex-HRD Corp chief warns against cutting training
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 18 — Corporate Malaysia must keep investing in its people to get real value from artificial intelligence (AI), Green Packet Bhd managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Shahul Hameed Shaik Dawood said as PEOPLElogy Berhad opened its Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference 2026 yesterday. PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee said: “Datuk Shahul has said what every leader in this room needs to hear. “Being AI ready is not about being technical.

items.title: ‘This has never happened before’: Negeri Sembilan has no rulebook for a menteri besar who quits, says state secretary
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 18 — The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office has yet to receive any official notification or letter from Datuk Ismail Lasim regarding his resignation as Menteri Besar. State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said the office only learnt that Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, had stepped down through a statement on social media on November 16. Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir graced the event, which was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud.

items.title: Court of Appeal reserves decision on Penang tycoon Tan Kok Ping’s bid to overturn RM350,000 defamation award to Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — The Court of Appeal today reserved its decision on businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping’s appeal against a High Court ruling ordering him to pay RM350,000 in damages to Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow for defamation. On December 3, 2024, the Penang High Court ordered Tan to pay RM350,000 in damages after finding that remarks he made at a press conference on October 18, 2023, were defamatory. In his submissions before the Court of Appeal today, Kirubakaran argued that the High Court judge had erred in law and fact in finding the three words defamatory.

items.title: Court of Appeal reinstates 13-year jail term and caning for 64-year-old convicted of raping teen in Rompin four years ago
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — The Court of Appeal today reinstated the 13-year jail sentence and four strokes of the cane imposed on an elderly man for raping a 19-year-old woman four years ago. Justice Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, who sat with Datuk Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly, made the unanimous decision after allowing the prosecution’s appeal to set aside the Kuantan High Court’s decision to acquit Nasir Sharif, 64, the respondent. However, the Kuantan High Court on January 13, 2026, acquitted Nasir after allowing his appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision.

items.title: Chips, batteries and optical tech: Anwar’s investment pitch in Shenzhen, Fastprint eyes PCB plant in Kulim
items.summary: SHENZHEN, Nov 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met with representatives of China-linked technology and electronics manufacturing companies Fastprint and Fastrain here today to discuss developments and proposed investments in Malaysia. Anwar said the investments should bring direct benefits to the people through high-skilled job opportunities, technology transfers and greater participation by local companies in the supply chain. Anwar said the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) would continue to follow up with the companies and relevant agencies to facilitate project implementation and ensure that investment commitments translate into industrial development and economic opportunities for the people.

items.title: Court of Appeal says sentence too light, raises Arabic teacher’s jail term to 10 years for sexual assault of schoolgirl
items.summary: “We set aside the sentence imposed by the High Court and substitute it with eight years’ imprisonment for the offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and a further two years’ imprisonment under Section 16(1) of the same Act, together with two strokes of the cane. “The court also orders the respondent to undergo counselling and police supervision for two years upon completion of his prison sentence,” said Justice Mohamed Zaini. The panel dismissed Ahnaf Afiq’s appeal against his conviction and sentence imposed by the Muar High Court on March 11, 2026.

items.title: Sarawak’s election fever rising: 517 forms sold, 10 days ahead of nomination day
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 18 — With 10 days to go before nomination day on November 28, preparations for the 13th Sarawak State Election are gathering pace, with 517 nomination forms sold as of yesterday. Sarawak State Election Director Abang Noraffian Abang Ibrahim said sales of the forms, which began on November 6, included 390 purchased directly at the Sarawak State Election Office counter. On October 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg announced the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective October 26, to pave the way for the 13th state election.

items.title: Unclothed man found dead at Pandan Jaya LRT carpark, police appeal for info
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The body of an unclothed, unidentified man was discovered in the carpark of the Pandan Jaya LRT station this morning. Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid confirmed the discovery, The Star reported this evening. A medical assistant from Hospital Ampang later confirmed that the man was dead.

items.title: Malaysian banks step up cybersecurity investment after recent attacks, says BNM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is stepping up supervisory measures and regulatory requirements to ensure financial institutions remain resilient against evolving cyber threats, including their ability to detect, respond to and recover from cyber incidents, Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. He said financial institutions had also made significant investments to strengthen their cybersecurity defences following recent cyberattacks. “We also work closely with the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and financial institutions to strengthen the sector’s cyber preparedness, resilience and operational readiness,” he said at a press conference on third-quarter gross domestic product performance today.

items.title: Azalina demands explanation over leaked Najib Pardons Board minutes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has issued a statement calling on the relevant authorities to explain how the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes that discussed Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon had been made public. Speaking as Umno’s information chief, Azalina questioned if the minutes are officially declassified, when and by whom. “For documents with official secret status, the decision to declassify them must be made by the authority under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972 [Act 88] according to the applicable procedures,” said Azalina, who is also minister for law and institutional reforms.

items.title: Too early to gauge impact of new US chip curbs on Malaysia, says BNM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The impact of the latest United States (US) restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres is still too early to assess, as developments surrounding the matter are still unfolding, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour. He said BNM concurred with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry’s (Miti) stance that Malaysia would continue to engage with the relevant authorities on the matter. Abdul Rasheed also emphasised that diversification remained a key strategy guiding Malaysia’s developments across various sectors, including date centres.

items.title: KPDN: No significant price hikes in essentials, public transport after targeted fuel subsidies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The implementation of targeted fuel subsidies has not resulted in a significant increase in the prices of essential goods or public transport fares, based on monitoring by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN). According to the ministry, the distribution of subsidies through the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) and Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) took into account their potential impact on the transportation costs of essential goods, land public transport fares, as well as ferry and passenger boat services. “Based on monitoring of essential goods prices and public transport fares, no significant price increases have been reported following the implementation of targeted fuel subsidies, which began on June 10, 2024, for SKDS and September 30, 2025, for SKPS,” the ministry said in a written reply published on the official Parliament website.

items.title: PM Anwar credits govt measures for Malaysia’s strong growth despite West Asia crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Madani government’s proactive measures to safeguard economic stability and ensure fuel supply amid the West Asia crisis have helped Malaysia maintain strong economic growth despite external uncertainties, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He emphasised that the government’s decisive action in addressing the West Asia crisis, supported by reforms implemented under the Madani Economy framework, has strengthened the country’s economic resilience. He said the Madani government remained optimistic about the country’s economic prospects but stayed cautious about geopolitical tensions and climate-related risks weighing on the global economy as Malaysia heads into 2027.

items.title: PAC urges govt to break monopoly on vehicle supply concessions
items.summary: PAC chairperson Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the categories that could be opened to other companies include vans, buses, four-wheel-drive vehicles, ambulances, and motorcycles. This was one of three additional recommendations by the PAC to improve the management of government concession vehicles, following the tabling of PAC’s Follow-Up Action Report on the Management of Government Vehicles under Concession Agreements in the Dewan Rakyat today. She noted that the PAC’s investigation into the management of government vehicles — under a 15-year concession agreement 2 between the Finance Ministry (MOF) and Spanco — revealed weaknesses in contract management and governance practices.

items.title: Umno denounces leak of Najib pardon minutes as ‘provocation’, singles out Tony Pua
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Umno has condemned the circulation of purported Federal Territories Pardons Board minutes concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon, denouncing the leak as a deliberate “provocation” to undermine the royal prerogative and demanding that Putrajaya clarify whether the Yang di-Pertuan Agong gave royal consent for their disclosure. In a statement today, Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party viewed the dissemination of the confidential records with “deep regret” and treated the matter “seriously”. He directed pointed criticism at former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua, who uploaded screenshots of the purported board minutes onto his personal Facebook account.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB to seek audience with Tuanku Muhriz as 10 sacked excos drop lawsuit
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 18 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim is scheduled to seek a fresh audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir this Friday to map out the state assembly calendar and explore solutions for 10 sacked executive council members. A source said that the high-stakes consultation will mark their second royal engagement this week, following an audience granted yesterday at Istana Hinggap after Barisan Nasional (BN) publicly claimed that the Juasseh assemblyman had tendered his resignation, FMT reported. “He will continue performing his duties as menteri besar as usual,” the source said, adding that Ismail and Tuanku Muhriz are expected to examine the potential reappointment of the 10 dismissed councillors to restore executive functionality and ensure the state administration can govern effectively.

items.title: Asean spoke with one voice to Trump on bloc’s common position, says Anwar
items.summary: SHENZHEN, Nov 18 — Asean member states are committed to continuing to work closely together and upholding the centrality of the regional bloc, particularly through engagement with United States President Donald Trump, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the consensus formed a common position conveyed to Trump during the Asean-United States Special Summit in Manila yesterday. He said this when asked to comment on the meeting between Asean member states and Trump.

items.title: No audience with Sultan: Perak MB office refutes viral state assembly dissolution claims
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 18 — The Perak Menteri Besar’s Office has dismissed viral social media claims alleging that Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad had sought an audience with the Sultan of Perak to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly, describing the rumours as completely unfounded. The state administration revealed that it had detected manipulated graphics styled to mimic authentic television news broadcasts, alongside the recirculating of outdated news reports designed to sow public confusion over the legal status of the state assembly. Saying that it views the spread of disinformation seriously, particularly narratives that misrepresent the royal institution and compromise state administration, the office confirmed that it has sought police intervention.

items.title: MCMC asks Anthropic to clarify report on Claude-powered voter targeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Malaysia is seeking information from US artificial intelligence firm Anthropic over the alleged use of its technology in a political influence operation targeting Malaysian voters, the government has said. Anthropic said in a report issued in September it had uncovered a suspected AI-powered campaign meant to disrupt elections in the Southeast Asian nation. The ministry said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission was “seeking further information and clarification from Anthropic regarding the report”, and would then “determine appropriate follow-up actions”.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues nationwide storm warning until 6pm ahead of evening rush hour
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a nationwide thunderstorm warning for this afternoon, forecasting torrential downpours, lightning, and gusty winds across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Sarawak, and Labuan until 6.00pm today. In Perak, stormy conditions are expected across seven districts, spanning Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kinta, and Kampar. In the central and southern corridors, adverse weather spans the Klang Valley and southern industrial heartlands, blanketing eight Selangor districts: Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Klang, and Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Stay out of state affairs, Zahid tells Negeri Sembilan MB’s son after scapegoat claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has warned the family of Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim against interfering in state affairs, after the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar’s son publicly questioned the coalition’s decision to announce his father’s purported resignation. “This is a matter concerning the state administration. This is a matter concerning the menteri besar, not his father, Ismail Lasim,” Zahid said.

items.title: AG and FT minister fought Najib’s conditional pardon, leaked Pardons Board minutes show
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh both registered firm objections to granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon for house arrest during the Sept 18 Pardons Board meeting, according to purported minutes of the confidential session leaked online. The minister in the Prime Minister’s Department overseeing Federal Territories, an executive portfolio held by Yeoh, endorsed the attorney-general’s dissenting position, reaffirming her prior opposition to the pardon. The King subsequently ruled that Yeoh must sign the order as the minister responsible for Federal Territories administration.

items.title: Sabah Immigration busts nomadic online fraud syndicate in Kota Kinabalu
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 18 — Twelve Chinese nationals operating a cross-border online financial scam syndicate from a residential bungalow in Damai have been arrested by immigration enforcement officers, the Sabah Immigration Department confirmed today. “During the operation, JIM Sabah seized 153 mobile phones of various models, 11 computers, one central processing unit (CPU), a printer, 13 routers, seven chargers, 22 SIM cards and three passports,” said Sabah Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof during a Press conference today. Enforcement teams also confiscated assorted foreign currencies scattered across the premises.

items.title: Ten former Negeri Sembilan exco members withdraw constitutional crisis suit
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 18 — The High Court here was informed today that 10 former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members have withdrawn their originating summons against the State Secretary and two other parties over the constitutional crisis in the state, without liberty to file afresh. High Court Judge Roz Mawar Rozain allowed the withdrawal after being informed by the plaintiffs’ counsel, Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, that his clients had decided to withdraw the entire suit, including the application under the Federal Court’s original jurisdiction. The court also ordered the plaintiffs to pay costs of RM20,000 to the first defendant, the State Secretary; RM20,000 to the second defendant, the State Government; and RM8,000 to the third defendant, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU), subject to allocator.

items.title: Data centre boom powers Malaysia’s Q3 GDP to 5.5pc expansion, DOSM says
items.summary: The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) reported today that gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 5.5 per cent year-on-year in the July-to-September period, moderating slightly from the 6.0 per cent pace recorded in the second quarter. The technology spillover also reinforced high-value manufacturing, which expanded 7.7 per cent. Gross fixed capital formation (GFCF), which measures spending on productive physical assets, climbed 8.1 per cent, nearly doubling the 4.6 per cent registered in the second quarter.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng questions RM210m annual Perak water payment, warns Penang tariffs could surge past RM7
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 18 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has launched a scathing critique of Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and state exco member Zairil Khir Johari, accusing the state leadership of disappointing residents by refusing to justify a 40-year water pact that requires Penang to pay Perak RM210 million annually, even if zero treated water is delivered. The mammoth commitment comprises RM8.4 billion in fixed capacity charges and an estimated RM16.2 billion in variable volumetric supply charges. Beyond the fixed RM8.4 billion commitment, Lim cautioned that escalating supply charges could trigger punishing tariff hikes for Penang domestic and industrial consumers.

items.title: Two dead, one injured after Honda Civic crashes with poultry truck on Gerik-Jeli Highway
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 18 — Two people were killed and another injured when the car they were travelling in collided with a lorry transporting chickens on the East-West Highway (JRTB) between Gerik and Jeli, near Gerik, early this morning. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 12.52 am, prompting the dispatch of personnel from the Gerik Fire and Rescue Station, located about 60 kilometres from the scene. Personnel then carried out rescue operations using specialised equipment and a stretcher to extricate the victims.

items.title: Police shoot dead robbery suspect linked to 24 cases in Chow Kit hotel raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — A wanted criminal linked to at least 24 robberies across the capital was shot dead after opening fire on a joint police strike team during a pre-dawn raid on a hotel in Chow Kit today. The operation unfolded around 2.00am when detectives from the Special Investigation Division (D9) of the Kuala Lumpur police contingent, supported by Bukit Aman personnel, tracked down the suspect's hideout and breached the hotel room, Berita Harian reported. Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the armed suspect resisted arrest and immediately discharged his weapon towards the entry team.

items.title: Zahid says he ‘believes’ decision was made after Ismail Lasim’s royal audience last night, palace to announce outcome
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 18 — All decisions and official announcements regarding the resignation status of Datuk Ismail Lasim and the candidate for the new Menteri Besar will be left entirely to the discretion of the Negeri Sembilan Palacesaid Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said further details on the matter would have to await an announcement by the palace. So, I believe that something has been jointly decided by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and Datuk Ismail (during yesterday’s audience),” he said.
